g.text: Architecture Evolution — MHA -> MQA -> GQA -> MLA -> CLA -> YOCO -> SSM -> Hybrid
Explained on: Beyond → Attention variants compared · sessions 04 MQA, 05 GQA, 06 MLA | M_KV = 2 * L * B * T * H_kv * d_h * S
1 · Timeline: each step attacks a different term of M_KV
COST: max K/V diversity; huge KV, every
IDEA: groups of 4 Q heads share KV
COST: some sharing; uptrain from MHA with
COST: decoupled RoPE; retrain or convert
IDEA: adjacent layers share one KV
COST: layers lose private KV; retrain
CACHE: fixed state, independent of T
ATTACKS: KV only in some layers

Mental model: GQA attacks head redundancy | MLA attacks representation redundancy | CLA/YOCO attack layer redundancy | SSM/hybrid attack the assumption that every layer needs an explicit token-level KV cache.
2 · Per-layer KV pictures (8 layers shown for illustration; real models have L = 32 ... 80)
A MHA / GQA / MQA: every layer owns KV
GQA/MQA only make each copy thinner (H_kv), never fewer.
Cache grows with T in EVERY layer.
B MLA: every layer owns a tiny LATENT
teal = c^KV (512) + k^R (64) = 576 elements / token / layer
Still 8 caches: MLA shrinks the width, not the layer count.
C CLA: adjacent layers share one KV
8 layers -> 4 KV copies (50%); odd layers have no W_k / W_v.
Paper: ~2x smaller than the MQA baseline at near-equal accuracy.
attacks L in M_KV (dashed red = reuse).
self-decoder (L/2): efficient attention, small constant cache (teal).
cross-decoder (L/2): ALL layers read ONE global KV (green).
You Only Cache Once: global KV is not duplicated per layer.
E Pure SSM / linear: state instead of KV
s_t = f(s_{t-1}, x_t): fixed-size state per layer, independent of T.
But a compressed summary: exact 'what was the 5th number in paragraph 72?' retrieval is
Per 8-layer block only 1 layer keeps a KV cache -> 12.5% of layers.
Most sequence processing is done by cheap Mamba state.
~75% of layers recurrent (cheap), 25% full attention (exact retrieval).
48 layers = 12 blocks of 4 -> only 12 layers keep KV.
KV memory ~ 0.25x of a full-attention stack of the same depth.
Capacity = cheap memory + selective exact retrieval
You do not need 100% full attention: maybe 25% of layers can provide the expensive
high-fidelity retrieval and 75% can use state-based processing (Qwen3-Next 3:1; Jamba
3 · Attention vs recurrent state: exact retrieval vs compressed memory
Full attention: Q reads every cached K/V directly (O_t = softmax(Q_t K_{1:t}^T / sqrt(d_h)) V_{1:t})
Exact token-level retrieval (K_{72,5}) but expensive KV: bytes read per token ~ T * H_kv * d_h.
Recurrent state: tokens are folded into one small state s_t = f(s_{t-1}, x_t)
Efficient (O(1) memory in T) but the state is a lossy summary: weak at arbitrary retrieval of one specific token.
Attention budget in a hybrid (8 layers shown):
KV needed in 2 of 8 layers (25%) -> M_KV_hybrid ~ 0.25 * M_KV_full
(plus a fixed-size recurrent state in the other 75%)
see the tree on the left
GQA | MQA | MLA | CLA | hybrid SSM
paged KV | prefix cache | KV quantization | offloading
FlashAttention | FlashMLA | fused kernels | Tensor Cores
continuous batching | speculative decoding | prefill/decode disaggregation | tensor parallelism | expert parallelism
VRAM capacity | HBM/GDDR bandwidth | Tensor Core throughput | NVLink | PCIe
L1 serving: Paged, FlashAttn, KV quant,
cont. batching, prefix cache - no retrain
Modern LLM inference engineering = reduce the information that must move through the memory
hierarchy without removing what the model needs for high-quality retrieval.
